title: Elephants Think Before They Act - Nautilus
gist: A PLOS One study by Thai and U.S. researchers tested inhibitory control in 16 Asian elephants at Thailand’s National Elephant Institute, probing a self-regulation capacity previously documented in primates and some birds but not known in elephants.

insights.claim: Inhibitory control — resisting an impulse in order to make a better decision — is documented in humans, other primates and some birds, but was not previously known in elephants.
insights.so_what: Establishes the baseline the new study is moving: comparative cognition keeps widening the set of species credited with executive function.
insights.quote: This “inhibitory control” is also found in other primates and some birds. Such ability to self-regulate is not, however, known in elephants.
insights.locator: As humans, we value rational decision-making
insights.speaker: Devin Reese

insights.claim: Researchers from Thailand and the U.S. presented a problem-solving task to 16 Asian elephants (Elephas maximus), eight males and eight females, housed at the National Elephant Institute in Thailand, publishing in PLOS One.
insights.so_what: A 16-animal sample at a single facility is the practical ceiling for large-mammal cognition work — read effect claims with that constraint in mind.
insights.locator: In a study published today in the journal PLOS One
insights.speaker: Devin Reese

insights.claim: The standard test of animal self-regulation is whether the subject takes an immediately offered reward at the cost of a better later one — framed here as whether an elephant will grab a proffered banana even if it means missing out on a better meal later.
insights.so_what: A single, portable task design that makes executive function comparable across species — and an intuitive model for discount rates in any decision system.
insights.quote: Will an elephant, for example, grab a proffered banana even if it means missing out on a better meal later on?
insights.locator: Will an elephant, for example, grab a proffered banana
insights.speaker: Devin Reese
